plan: This is a second-price auction with 3 bidders and independent private values from $0-$49. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) when you win, bidding your value ensures you win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and avoid losses. Bidding higher than value risks overpaying; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $26.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value, since you pay the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you win). Bidding above your value risks paying more than the item is worth if I win against a bid between my value and my bid; bidding below reduces chances of winning profitable trades. Therefore, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (I win if highest, but pay the second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. If I bid above value, I risk winning at a price exceeding my value (negative profit). If I bid below value, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $24.
